(Japanese: '''ファイナルⅠ　「激流」''' ''The Finals I: "Torrent"'') is the 129th episode of ''[[Pokémon Journeys: The Series]]'', and the 1,214th episode of the [[Pokémon animated series]]. It first aired in Japan on October 21, 2022, in Canada on March 18, 2023, in South Africa on March 28, 2023, in the United Kingdom on April 11, 2023, in Australia on May 3, 2023, and in the United States on June 23, 2023. {{spoilers}} ==Blurb== Following an emergency communication from Project Mew, Goh is off to Hoenn, while Ash battles Leon in the Masters Eight Tournament finals. It’s a six-on-six Full Battle, and although each Trainer can typically use Dynamax, a Z-Move, or Mega Evolution only once, Leon insists that Ash use all three. Leon first sends out his Cinderace, who spars with Pikachu, and then Leon’s Inteleon battles Ash’s Gengar. After Gigantamaxing, Gengar takes down Inteleon, but Leon’s Mr. Rime manages to defeat it. Ash and Leon are now back on equal footing, and this massive battle promises to keep going strong! ==Plot== [[File:Ash party JN.png|thumb|250px|left|Ash with his Pokémon before their battle against Leon]] Following an [[JN127|urgent summons]] by [[Project Mew]], [[Goh]] has arrived in [[Slateport City]] in [[Hoenn]], where he is quickly reunited with his fellow Chasers [[Horace]] and {{Gary}}. Gary understands that Goh must feel disappointed for missing the finals of the [[Masters Eight Tournament]], but Goh assures he's fine, given that he and Ash promised to smile the next time they meet. As the three of them move to join [[Professor Amaranth]], [[Danika]], and [[Quillon]] at Project Mew's mobile laboratory, Goh wishes Ash good luck. Back in [[Galar]], Ash is also wishing Goh good luck as he enters [[Wyndon Stadium]]. In his dressing room, he gives a pep talk to his [[Party|team]] to get them pumped up, only to be interrupted by the unexpected appearance of {{an|Dawn}} and [[Chloe]], who have come to cheer for him in person. In his own dressing room, {{an|Leon}} muses how this occasion reminds him of his first-ever {{pkmn|battle}} against [[Sonia]] as a child. The entire stadium is filled with excitement as the finals are about to begin, with [[Dawn's Piplup]] even donning the cheerleader outfit he used while cheering for Ash during [[Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl|his Sinnoh travels]]. Eager to join in, [[Chloe's Eevee]] also starts waving a pom-pom, which Chloe finds cute. Finally, the two finalists enter the field: Ash, the first {{pkmn|Champion}} of [[Alola]] and a native of [[Kanto]], who defeated Hoenn Champion {{an|Steven Stone}} in the quarterfinals and [[Sinnoh]] Champion {{an|Cynthia}} in the semifinals; and Leon, the reigning Monarch and the undefeated Galar Champion. The cheering Ash gets is enough to make {{TRT}} give up on their broadcast and focus on cheering for him as well. In the stands, [[Hop]] is joined by Sonia to cheer for Leon. Ash and Leon are both feeling excited about finally getting to face each other in a serious battle. As usual, [[Gym guide|Dan]] starts explaining the rules, declaring the match to be a six-on-six [[Full Battle]] with no time limit or [[Recall|switching]] restrictions. However, his usual explanation of only one of either [[Mega Evolution]], [[Z-Move]]s, or [[Dynamax]] being allowed per {{pkmn|Trainer}} is interrupted by Leon, who wants to see Ash at his full power in this climactic battle and urges him to use all three of them so he can face and beat all of them with his own full power. The entire stadium unanimously agrees to this, including Hop. Chloe, intimidated by the sound of the roaring crowd, asks Dawn what that means, and she says that it will be a great battle. After a brief discussion with the [[World Coronation Series]] management, Dan officiates this exception of the usual rules, which Ash also approves. With this established, Ash and Leon send out their first Pokémon, Ash leading with {{AP|Pikachu}} and Leon starting off with {{p|Cinderace}}. At Dan's starting signal, both Pokémon launch their first [[move]]s. Cinderace's {{m|Scorching Sands}} hits faster than Pikachu's {{m|Thunderbolt}} and deals {{DL|Type|Type effectiveness|supereffective}} [[damage]], though Pikachu's attack still goes off and scores a hit. To Ash's shock, however, Cinderace shrugs off the hit without as much as a hint of damage. Leon reveals that his Cinderace has the {{a|Libero}} [[Ability]], which [[Type change|changes its type]] to match the [[type]] of the move it uses, meaning that, at the moment, Cinderace is a {{t|Ground}} type. Seeing that Pikachu is at a clear type disadvantage now, Ash recalls his buddy while Leon does the same with Cinderace. [[File:Dawn and Chloe.png|thumb|250px|Dawn and Chloe in the audience together]] For their respective second Pokémon, Ash and Leon choose {{AP|Gengar}} and {{p|Inteleon}}, making Ash feel like he's battling Goh's partners. Inteleon outspeeds Gengar's {{m|Shadow Ball}} with {{m|Snipe Shot}}, before proceeding to swat the attack apart with its tail and prepare a {{m|Dark Pulse}}. While Gengar manages to avoid the attack by hiding in its own shadow, Leon remains unfaltering and has Inteleon use {{m|Aqua Jet}} while spinning in place, creating a spiral of water. Ash and Dawn both recognize this tactic as [[Counter Shield]], which [[JN123|Ash used against Cynthia in the semifinals]] and impressed Leon enough for him to copy it. With Ash's own tactic being turned against him, Gengar is in a dire strait, but eventually, it manages to break free and uses {{m|Will-O-Wisp}}, evaporating the water and covering the field in a cloud of steam. While Inteleon is momentarily blinded, Ash recalls Gengar and [[Gigantamax]]es it just as the mist fades away. What follows is a clash between Gengar's {{m|G-Max Terror}} and Inteleon's dual Snipe Shot, with both sides succeeding in hitting the other. Due to G-Max Terror's effect, Inteleon becomes [[Escape prevention|unable to switch out]], though Hop remains confident that his big brother can manage it. The next exchange of attacks comes in the form of a {{m|Max Ooze}} from Gengar and a dual Dark Pulse from Inteleon. While Inteleon does its best to avoid the [[Max Move]] and succeeds in landing a [[critical hit]] with Dark Pulse in the middle of Gengar's mouth, it still ends up being hit, while Gengar returns to normal size as a result of the critical hit. Observing Inteleon, Dan declares it [[Fainting|unable to battle]], giving Ash the first knockout of the finals and sparking celebration both in the crowd and amongst {{cat|Ash's Pokémon}} at [[Professor Oak's Laboratory]]. Recalling Inteleon, Leon promises to build up on the work it did and declares he'll catch up to Ash. In the crowd, Sonia notices how Leon is getting fired up. For his third Pokémon, Leon chooses {{p|Mr. Rime}}, while Ash sticks with Gengar and orders a {{m|Sludge Bomb}}. Leon counters with {{m|Freeze-Dry}}, which not only freezes and shatters the Sludge Bombs but also freezes the battlefield and covers Gengar in frost. Gengar suddenly shivers, which also occurs with Mr. Rime, making Ash smirk. A failed attempt at using Freeze-Dry again confirms Leon's suspicion: Gengar's {{a|Cursed Body}} Ability has activated, temporarily disabling Freeze-Dry. However, the first Freeze-Dry was still enough to leave Gengar {{status|freeze|frozen}}, giving Leon the opportunity to have Mr. Rime set up {{m|Psychic Terrain}} and attack his immobilized opponent with a powered-up {{m|Expanding Force}}, defeating Gengar and evening the playing field. While Ash recalls Gengar, Leon declares that he's dedicating this victory to Inteleon, reminding Ash that, in a Full Battle like this, the important thing is to build up damage on the opponent and
